subject: Hosted API rate structure: sensitivity analysis and bucket proposals
messages:
From: Susan Keller <susan.keller@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-05 09:12 -0700
Subject: Pricing: need clearer tier options for hosted API

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the overview last week. Procurement is asking for a rate card that shows how per-token effective price moves across realistic usage bands for our projected Q3–Q4 MAU. We can share a simple forecast (attached) but need two things from Redwood: a) a set of 3–4 tiered pricing buckets with clear breakpoints, and b) a sensitivity table that maps monthly token consumption to an effective $/1M tokens across those buckets.

High-level constraints: AtlasHealth expects big seasonality during Q4 (peak in November), and we need both sustained throughput guarantees and an optional burst bucket. We are open to a blended/committed option if it simplifies procurement, but procurement will want rollover or fair-credit mechanics (they flagged this).

Can your team produce a short sensitivity analysis and a proposed-ratecard we can share with procurement by EOD 2026-06-12? I attached our rough MAU/usage forecast.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Keller
Head of Platform Integrations
AtlasHealth

Attachment: atlas_mau_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx (xlsx, 125KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Keller <susan.keller@atlashealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05 11:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing: need clearer tier options for hosted API

Hi Susan — thanks for the forecast, that’s helpful. I’m looping in Ben (sales) and Lauren (pricing ops) so we can turn around a concise sensitivity table. Quick callouts up front:

- We typically publish a base hosted-hosted list rate and then provide volume break discounts at 3 breakpoints. For AtlasHealth size/seasonality I think 4 buckets will be clearer: 0–50M, 50–250M, 250–1B, >1B monthly tokens.
- We can offer a blended committed option (12-month commit) that buys ~10–20% lower effective price plus a Q4 burst pool you pay for on consumption and can draw from. Rollover credits are negotiable but we usually cap them to one quarter.
- For procurement: we can include a minimum sustained throughput SLA with an auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant if peak capacity is exceeded.

I attached a working draft (proposed-ratecard-v2.pdf) and a usage breakout CSV for scenario runs. Can you confirm the monthly token windows in the forecast are the ones you want modeled (sheet "MonthlyTokens") and whether Atlas would consider a 12-month committed spend? If not, we’ll prepare a pure consumption-tier table as well.

Deliverable: sensitivity table (effective $/1M tokens by month across 3 scenarios: no-commit, 12mo-commit, 12mo-commit+Q4-burst) + short summary of credit/rollover terms. We’ll aim to get that to you by 2026-06-08.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-ratecard-v2.pdf (pdf, 210KB); usage-breakout-scenarios.csv (csv, 58KB)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-06 08:30 -0700
Subject: RE: Pricing: need clearer tier options for hosted API

Karthik / Ben — internal notes while we build the sensitivity table:

- Margin guardrails: for AtlasHealth scale, target blended gross margin >= 52% at their mid-case. That implies we need about ~12–15% incremental discount between 50–250M and 250–1B buckets if we keep list close to current public levels.
- Rollover approach: suggest 1-quarter rollover credits capped at 25% of committed volume; this is palatable to procurement and reduces year-end rollover risk.
- Burst pool: model both a paid burst ($/1M tokens at +20% over committed rate) and an optional pre-purchased burst pool (one-time purchase that lowers per-burst cost). Lean toward paid burst for simplicity.
- Minimum commit: recommend a 6–9 month ramp for counting toward commit for new customers; for Atlas we can offer a phasing schedule if they want lower initial liability.

I’ll run three scenarios against the spreadsheet and output the effective $/1M table. Ben — can you confirm whether we want to include a short-term promotional credit (e.g., 10% first 3 months) to smooth adoption? If so, we’ll add that as scenario C.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Pricing Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Susan Keller <susan.keller@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasHealth Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-08 15:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing: need clearer tier options for hosted API

Karthik / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the working draft. Atlas prefers the committed+burst approach if the effective blended price in the mid-case (our projected monthly tokens) drops by at least 15% vs pure consumption. Procurement also confirmed that a 1-quarter rollover cap is acceptable.

Requests before procurement will sign off:
- A sensitivity table that maps our monthly consumption forecast to effective $/1M tokens for these scenarios: pure consumption, 12mo commit (with 1-quarter rollover), 12mo commit + paid burst. Please include the promotional credit option if you think it materially helps our Q3 adoption.
- A short paragraph describing the SLA around sustained throughput (target p95 latency, and guaranteed sustained throughput) and what happens if we exceed reserved throughput during peak — specifically how the fallback model works and any cost implications.
- Final proposed-ratecard PDF we can attach to the PO.

We need final materials by EOD 2026-06-12 to get legal/procurement review in time for the CFO runbook. Thanks again — attaching the forecast sheet for clarity.

Best,
Susan Keller
Head of Platform Integrations
AtlasHealth

Attachment: atlas_mau_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx (xlsx, 125KB)
